citations.title: Zoe Yujnovich Appointed CEO of National Grid

sentences.quote: Yujnovich will join the National Grid Board as chief executive designate on September 1 and will be appointed chief executive on November 17.
sentences.text: Zoe Yujnovich became chief executive of National Grid plc on 17 November 2025, having joined the board on 1 September and succeeded John Pettigrew, who retired after 10 years in post.

She came from Shell, where she was director of Integrated Gas and Upstream until the end of March 2025, when the division was split into separate Integrated Gas and Upstream units; since joining Shell in 2014 she had also been EVP Oil Sands Operations and chairman of Shell Australia.
Before Shell she spent almost two decades at Rio Tinto, including as president and chief executive of the Iron Ore Company of Canada.
She holds an executive MBA from the University of Utah (2004) and a Bachelor of Engineering (Hons) from the University of Western Australia (1995), and is also a non-executive director of Unilever.

sentences.text: Zoe Yujnovich became chief executive on 17 November 2025, having joined the board as chief executive designate on 1 September 2025, succeeding John Pettigrew, who retired from the board and the role on 16 November 2025 after nearly a decade.

sentences.quote: The new structure, which takes effect on 1 September, will see the geographic leaders supported by dedicated global teams for capital delivery and technology and innovation, with the executive committee cut from 13 members to eight.
sentences.text: In August 2026 the company announced an overhaul of its operating structure from 1 September, grouping businesses under single UK and US leaders and cutting the executive committee from 13 members to eight.
Cordi O'Hara was named President, UK; Sally Librera interim President, US, pending a search; Carl Trowell President of Global Capital; and Alice Delahunty Chief Technology and Innovation Officer.

citations.title: National Grid Appoints Zoe Yujnovich as New Chief Executive to Lead the Next Phase of Growth

sentences.quote: Zoe joins National Grid from Shell plc ("Shell"), where she served as Integrated Gas and Upstream Director and was a member of the Executive Committee. Prior to Shell, Zoe held various senior positions at Rio Tinto, including President and CEO of the Iron Ore Company of Canada.
sentences.text: Zoe Yujnovich became chief executive in November 2025, succeeding John Pettigrew, who retired after nearly 10 years, following a board succession process; she joined from Shell, where she ran Integrated Gas and Upstream, and earlier led Rio Tinto's iron ore company in Canada.

Prior management pivoted to networks and funded around GBP 60 billion of capital investment over five years via a completed GBP 7 billion rights issue, which rebased the dividend by about 15% and was followed by a sharp share price fall.
Delivery has since reached record capital investment of GBP 11,576 million in 2025/26, up 21% at constant currency, with group return on equity of 9.8% against 9.0%.

sentences.quote: National Grid is embarking on the largest investment programme in our history, committing at least GBP 70 billion over the next five years
sentences.text: National Grid plans to invest at least 70 billion pounds over the five years to 2030/31, its largest ever capital programme, targeting around 10% annual asset growth and 8-10% underlying EPS CAGR from a 78.0p baseline.
Roughly two-thirds of that programme is already covered by regulatory agreements and about three-quarters of delivery mechanisms are secured, giving unusual visibility.

sentences.quote: The recommended final dividend per share is 32.14p, bringing the total dividend for the year to 48.49p, a 3.8% increase in line with UK CPIH inflation.
sentences.text: The dividend policy aims to grow payout in line with UK CPIH inflation, with FY2026 dividend of 48.49p, up 3.8%.

sentences.quote: Nearly 80% of capital investment going into our Electricity Networks; Group mix moving towards 80%/20% electricity/gas by 2029.

sentences.text: National Grid has sharpened its focus on core regulated networks, completing the sale of National Grid Renewables and Grain LNG.
Demand-side support includes work on UK AI Growth Zones and readiness to connect 19 GW of additional demand under RIIO-T3.

thesis_pillars.text: National Grid plans to invest at least 70 billion pounds over the five years to 2030/31, its largest ever capital programme, targeting around 10% annual asset growth and 8-10% underlying EPS CAGR from a 78.0p baseline. The dividend policy aims to grow payout in line with UK CPIH inflation, with FY2026 dividend of 48.49p, up 3.8%. The portfolio is tilting toward electricity, with the group mix moving to about 80% electricity and 20% gas. National Grid has sharpened its focus on core regulated networks, completing the sale of National Grid Renewables and Grain LNG.
